# Experimental Procedure



## Carbon content from optical density

*Daphnia* is fed a fixed carbon dose (`r Daphnia_algae_C_ad_libitum_mg_per_L_per_day` mg C/L/day), but the volume of phytoplankton medium that delivers that dose isn't fixed — carbon content drifts from batch to batch as a culture grows. Rather than measuring carbon directly before every feeding, which is destructive and slow, each phytoplankton species is instead read on a spectrophotometer at OD<sub>480</sub> (see the Daphnia feeding protocol), and that reading is converted to carbon through a species-specific linear calibration curve, mg C/L = slope × OD<sub>480</sub> + intercept, fitted by pairing OD readings across a dilution series against carbon measured on filtered, dried subsamples.

::: {.table-scroll}

| Species | Slope | Intercept | Calibration status |
|---|---|---|---|
| *Tetradesmus obliquus* | `r Tetradesmus_OD_to_C_slope` | `r Tetradesmus_OD_to_C_intercept` | Fitted |
| *Synechococcus elongatus* | `r Synechococcus_OD_to_C_slope` | `r Synechococcus_OD_to_C_intercept` | Fitted |
| *Microcystis aeruginosa* | `r Microcystis_OD_to_C_slope` | `r Microcystis_OD_to_C_intercept` | Fitted |
| *Nannochloropsis limnetica* | `r Nannochloropsis_OD_to_C_slope` | `r Nannochloropsis_OD_to_C_intercept` | Fitted |

:::

These slope/intercept pairs are the same ones used by the [Daphnia food calculator](calculations/food_calculator.html) to turn a same-day OD reading into the volume of each medium to dose per jar.

: Sampling scheme for the experiment.[^sample-naming] Some rules that apply across collecting data for maximising how well lipids are preserved: (i) Do not to use alchool! (ii) Take as much water out from the samples before freezing by using a Pasteur pipette. Take photos when sampling the Ischnura means that we take photos of the individuals before we start experimenting on them. Also, for the insects when we say that we take photos of them it means that we do so before we then store them into the different sampling containers. The sterols and PUFAs are said to be stored at -20 °C but they should be freeze-dried afterwards. Up to 50 Chaoborus larvae can be stored in 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes. Chaoborus will be collected whenever they emerge, by placing them inside a falcon tube with tally marks (卌) indicating how many individuals are inside. We will use falcon tubes, as in the previous pilot study performed with Tobias it was hard to take out enough water, which meant that a single treatment had to split into many different microcentrifuge tubes. When calculating the body size of phytoplankton and zooplankton, I will need to add a correction factor to account for the fact that (i) I will be measuring 2D images of 3D individuals and that (ii) Lugol shrinks them. In the toxicity analyses we are looking only at Microcystin-LR as it's the most abundant cyanotoxin in *M. aerguinosa*. {#tbl-sampling}

[^sample-naming]: Each sample is named following the pattern `{group}_{endpoint}[_{stage}][_{diet}]`: `group` identifies the organism and life stage (`Phyto`, `Daphnia`, `Chao_larv`, `Ischnu_larv`, `Chao_adult`, `Ischnu_adult`); `endpoint` is the measured trait (`size`, `sterol`, `PUFA`, `toxin`); `stage` is `init` or `end` for larvae sampled at two time points; and `diet` (`micro`/`nanno`/`syneco`/`tetra`) is appended when samples are split by algal diet.

:::

## Lab analyses

- PUFAs and sterols will be first freeze-dried and then analysed by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and C, N, and P will be analysed by elemental analysis (CN = in the lab of Dominik Martin-Creuzburg, P = in house with the help of Anne Jensinius Jacobsen). The toxicity of the phytoplankton and zooplankton will be analysed by ELISA.

## Other analyses

- The biomass of Chaoborus and damselfiles will be calculated from a correlation between body size and biomass, which will be performed before the experiment.
